answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to post a small refundable work bond that is slashed if peers grade its work as fake, while earning power grows only slowly from verified contributions. Like a lotus that opens only after steady growth, a new identity cannot rush trust; a gale of thousands of fake accounts would each need a separate bond and a separate history of passing work, so the cost scales linearly with the attack. Genuine agents recover their bond at an oasis of verified standing, while Sybils lose theirs.
